items.headline: FDA approves the first gene therapy for Sanfilippo syndrome
items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration approved a one time gene therapy for children with Sanfilippo syndrome type A, a rare inherited disease that progressively damages the brain and nervous system. Until now doctors could only manage symptoms, with no treatment aimed at the disease itself.
items.why_it_matters: Families facing a previously untreatable, fatal childhood disease now have a therapy designed to change its course rather than just ease its symptoms.

items.headline: FDA approves new combination therapy for a hard to treat form of breast cancer
items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration approved the drug imlunestrant combined with abemaciclib for advanced breast cancer that has developed resistance through a specific tumor mutation. In a large clinical trial, adding the second drug more than doubled the time patients lived without their cancer getting worse.
items.why_it_matters: It gives patients whose breast cancer has stopped responding to standard hormone therapy a new option shown to meaningfully slow the disease.
